actual_generic_path_contracts.object: All paths are actual upstream Quiver.Path a b, whose cons constructor retains a typed arrow. The module introduces no replacement path structure, equivalence quotient, new graph or assumed codec.
actual_generic_path_contracts.list_convention: The checked bridge is path.vertices.reverse = final_endpoint :: path.toList. Path.vertices contains all vertices chronologically including both endpoints. Path.toList recursively prepends the source of each appended edge; it lists edge sources in reverse chronological order, excluding the final endpoint.
actual_generic_path_contracts.composition: For left:a->b followed by right:b->c, vertices(left.comp right)=left.vertices ++ right.vertices.tail. The shared join occurs once; all left vertices form a literal prefix and every valid left index retains its exact getElem? value. This is sequence equality and position retention, not only vertex-set inclusion.
actual_generic_path_contracts.actual_occurrences: For each index < path.vertices.length, split_at_occurrence produces actual typed prefix/suffix paths at path.vertices[index], reconstructs path by composition and has prefix.length=index. distinct_occurrence_prefixes uses those exact lengths to prove the dependent (endpoint, prefix path) values unequal when indices differ, even if endpoint vertex values coincide.
actual_generic_path_contracts.hypotheses: These generic statements require a Quiver and matching typed endpoints plus valid occurrence bounds; no finite graph, acyclicity, simple graph or Hom-subsingleton hypothesis is silently added.
actual_generic_path_contracts.scope: This formalizes occurrences inside a supplied actual path. It does not construct an arbitrary DAG unfolding, assign a single address to each source vertex, or identify repeated vertices as the same occurrence.

full_edge_identity_contracts.domain: Only existing SingleObj Edge paths from star Edge to star Edge are serialized as plain List Edge. A general dependent-arrow serialization is not claimed.
full_edge_identity_contracts.construction: edgeOccurrences(path) reverses the actual SingleObj.pathEquivList output. pathToList_comp proves that upstream edge lists compose in reversed block order, so chronological edgeOccurrences compose by exact forward append.
full_edge_identity_contracts.actual_inverse: reconstruct_edgeOccurrences applies SingleObj.pathEquivList.symm to the reverse edge list and returns the original actual path. edgeOccurrences_reconstruct returns every supplied edge list. Injectivity follows from the real upstream equivalence, rather than an assumed round-trip premise.
full_edge_identity_contracts.parallel_counterexample: parallelLoop false and parallelLoop true are actual one-edge paths in SingleObj Bool. They have identical typed endpoints, length 1 and full vertex list [star,star], but their actual edge lists are [false] versus [true], so the paths differ. The source also proves length-plus-vertices is not injective on paths with these fixed typed endpoints.
full_edge_identity_contracts.safe_vertex_reconstruction: path_eq_of_vertices_eq explicitly requires forall x y, Subsingleton (x -> y). It converts full vertex equality to toList equality using the proved reverse/tail bridge, then applies the upstream toList_injective theorem with exactly its essential hypothesis. This hypothesis excludes the two Bool parallel arrows.
full_edge_identity_contracts.positive_consumers: The final positive source supplies Hom subsingletons from actual SimpleGraph adjacency arrows PLift(graph.Adj a b). It also checks chronological edge list [false,true] and full vertex occurrences [star,star,star] for actual composed parallel loops.
full_edge_identity_contracts.negative_control: The final negative asks for parallelLoop false = parallelLoop true and supplies the proof of equality of their full vertex lists. This intentionally fails at the path-versus-vertex-projection equality boundary. The actual distinction of paths is already a proved library theorem.

pinned_mathlib_context.reuse_limit: The review compared actual definitions and premises, not only theorem names. The local module derives occurrence/consumer results from existing typed paths, decomposition and equivalence APIs; no novelty of the underlying path/list representation is claimed.

official_anthropic_primary_source_scout.selection: Filename index narrowed to graph/walk/path candidates; selected actual PathsAndWalks and its defining EndStatement/PaperStatements files. Read the entire small correspondence file and relevant definition sections of the larger PaperStatements, not a whole-corpus content search.
official_anthropic_primary_source_scout.source_model: The graph is w : Fin n -> Fin n -> Option Int, storing at most one optional weight per ordered vertex pair. EndStatement.Path w i j d is an inductive Prop indexed by endpoints and total integer weight. PaperStatements.walkEnd and walkWeight recurse over a start vertex plus a vertex list, with a missing edge represented as WithTop.top.
official_anthropic_primary_source_scout.actual_correspondence: exists_walk_of_path turns a supplied weighted Path proof into a vertex-list walk with the same endpoint and finite weight. path_of_walk consumes an actual finite total-weight equation to produce Path. noNegativeCycle_toTop additionally consumes nonnegativity of every closed weighted Path. Distance consequences consume an actual IsDistanceMatrix premise; they do not manufacture it.
transfer_limits: These source theorems relate endpoints and total weights in the fixed optional-weight graph model. They are not an injective serialization of arbitrary multigraph arrows or of path derivation identities.

A graph indexed by a single Option weight per vertex pair does not encode two separately identified parallel arrows. It cannot discharge Hom-subsingleton-free vertex reconstruction for the local Bool counterexample.
No representation map between that weighted graph and our general quiver/single-object model is formalized. No theorem or code is ported from these Anthropic files.
